SK1050 Use pattern matching instead of a test-and-cast

A conversion followed by a null check, a safe cast used only as a type test, or a negated type check is a pattern.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 7.0
Since1.3
ReSharperUsePatternMatching (resharper_use_pattern_matching_highlighting)
SupersedesIDE0019, IDE0078, IDE0083

Why

var b = x as Binary; if (b != null) converts, stores, and then asks whether the conversion worked — three steps for one question the language has had an answer to since C# 7. x is Binary b is one isinst, one variable, and a relationship the reader does not have to reconstruct from two adjacent statements. The same holds for (x as T) != null, which allocates a conversion result nobody wants in order to test a type, and for !(x is T), which reads as the negation of a question rather than as the question the code is actually asking.

Example

Instead of:

var binary = node as Binary;
if (binary != null) {
    Visit(binary.Left);
}

Write:

if (node is Binary binary) {
    Visit(binary.Left);
}

When it does not fire

⚠ This rule owns `IDE0019` (`as` followed by a null check), and it was `SK1015`'s claim until [#314]. SK1015 matches is T plus a cast and never fires on the as-plus-null-check shape at all — measured on one file holding both, where SK1015 reported only the is shape and this rule only the as one — so the claim named a rule that does not implement the concept, and EveryHostedDiagnostic_IsClaimedByAtMostOneRule meant it also blocked the rule that does. ⚠ The claim is attribution, not suppression: IDE0019 lands on the declaration and this rule reports at the null check one line below, so Supersession.Apply's exact (path, line, column) match never fires for the pair. ⚠ `SK1015` owns `is T` followed by a cast; this rule is the rest of the family and never restates it. Four shapes: an as conversion whose very next statement is an if testing it for null, a safe cast compared against null ((x as T) != null → x is T), a negated type test (!(x is T) → x is not T), and a type check that succeeds for every non-null value of the operand's own static type (s is object → s is not null). ⚠ The as-plus-null-check shape requires every reference to the local to be inside the if it guards: a pattern variable is not definitely assigned after the if, so a use below it would be CS0165, and an else branch is refused for the same reason. The conversion operand must be a chain of plain names, so nothing that could be evaluated for a side effect moves into a condition. ⚠ The tested type must be a reference type — x is int? is CS8116 — and a null comparison whose operand type declares operator == is left alone, because == there is not the reference test the pattern makes. ⚠ The two shapes that produce a not pattern are silent below C# 9 even though the rule's floor is C# 7, and every shape is silent inside an expression tree, where a pattern is CS8122, and where rewriting would change what the tree contains. ⚠ Not covered, and deliberately so: UseSwitchCasePatternVariable (a switch case that casts in its body), ConvertTypeCheckPatternToNullCheck, and the negated as guard (if (t == null) return;), which needs a reachability proof the other shapes do not.
